challenges.name: agent-loop-quiz
challenges.title: Read the loop: tool failures and parallel calls
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the support agent's loop: a tool timeout that ended the run, and a model request rejected after parallel calls.

questions.explanation: False. A failed tool call is information the model can act on: retry once (as in the replay, where the second list_orders succeeded), use another tool, ask the learner, or say it could not check and hand over. Feeding the failure back as a structured entry (code tool_failed and a short message) keeps the run going and leaves the decision to the model, while the loop still controls how often it may try (step limits, lesson 3.1). Ending the run turns every transient timeout into a failed ticket, which is what filled the human queue in the incident. Errors the model cannot fix, such as the model API rejecting the request or a bug in the loop, are the ones that should stop the run. The misconception is that stopping is always the safe default; for a read-only lookup it only makes the agent fail more often.

True. The model API (and the fake model in the exercise) requires one result for every tool call of the previous turn, in order. The loop recorded call_4 in the assistant message but appended nothing for it, so the next request is rejected before the model ever sees it. Appending { role: "tool", callId: "call_4", ok: false, error: { code: "invalid_arguments", message: "\"course_slug\" must be string" } } after call_3's result satisfies the protocol and tells the model exactly which argument to fix. The misconception is that an invalid call can simply be ignored; every call the model proposed needs an answer, even if the answer is an error.

challenges.name: agent-loop-fake-model
challenges.title: The agent loop, run against a scripted fake model
challenges.description: The CodeDev support agent runs one loop: ask the model for a turn, run the tool calls it proposes, append the results, repeat. Incident: the shipped loop ran only the first of two parallel calls (the model API then rejected the request: tool call call_4 has no matching tool result), let a tool timeout escape as an exception, and crashed on unknown tool names; 212 of 1,980 runs in one week ended in the fallback reply. Write runAgent(model, tools, task) with tools: Map<string, Tool>. Start the transcript with { role: "user", content: task } and repeat: (1) turn = model.next(transcript); do not catch errors thrown by model.next, let them propagate. (2) A turn { final } appends { role: "assistant", final } and returns { answer: final, transcript, stats }. (3) A turn { toolCall } is one call, { toolCalls } several calls proposed together. Give each call the id call_<n>, n counting from 1 over the whole run in the order proposed, append ONE message { role: "assistant", toolCalls: [{ id, name, args }, ...] }, then handle the calls in that order and append one tool message per call in the same order. A tool message is { role: "tool", callId, name, ok: true, result } or { role: "tool", callId, name, ok: false, error: { code, message } }: no tool with that name in the map: code unknown_tool, message unknown tool "<name>"; available tools: <tool names in map order, joined by ", ">. tool.validate(args) returns violations: code invalid_arguments, message the violations joined by "; ", and the tool does not run. tool.run(args) throws: code tool_failed, message the Error's message, a thrown string as is, any other value JSON.stringify'd. Otherwise ok: true with the returned value as result. A failing call never stops the run or the other calls of its turn. (4) Ask the model again. There is no step limit in this exercise; the fake model throws when asked for more than 50 turns. stats counts modelTurns (turns returned by model.next), toolCalls (calls proposed), executed (calls to tool.run, including the ones that threw), invalidArguments, unknownTools and toolFailures. The fake model in the runner returns its scripted turns in order (repeating the last one) and, like a real model API, throws if the transcript does not start with the task, does not hold one assistant message per earlier turn with the calls it proposed, reuses a call id, or does not answer every call of its previous turn in order. Input (stdin): { "task", "tools": [{ name, parameters, outcomes }], "script": ModelTurn[], "summary"?: true }. The runner prints the transcript (with summary: its length and a checksum), the answer, the stats and how often each tool ran, or error: <message> when runAgent throws. Do not change the types or the test runner.
hints: For each proposed call, which of four things happened: the tool does not exist, its arguments are invalid, it ran and threw, or it ran and returned? And whatever happened, what must the model find in the transcript before you ask it for the next turn?

Look at the order of your appends: the assistant message with all calls of the turn comes first, then exactly one tool message per call, without break or continue in between. Put the try/catch around tool.run only (not around model.next), keep the id counter outside the loop over turns, and check thrown values with instanceof Error and typeof before JSON.stringify.

A similar run on different input: the task "Where is my certificate?", tools get_certificate and list_courses, and a script of one turn with two calls (get_certificate { "course_slug": 7 } and send_email {}), then a final answer. The transcript is: the user task; one assistant message with call_1 get_certificate and call_2 send_email; a tool message for call_1 with error invalid_arguments and the validator's message; a tool message for call_2 with error unknown_tool listing get_certificate, list_courses; then the assistant's final answer. The stats show 2 model turns, 2 calls, 0 executed, 1 invalid, 1 unknown, 0 failed, and neither tool ran.
